about: The Flash-Next arsenal as data (the owner, 2026-10-01: stop collapsing the toolset). A lever counts as TRIED only when its FULL form has run. Partial forms are recorded as partial. plan_lint.py refuses a plan that names no levers, refuses unknown lever ids, and every placement prints the levers whose full form has never run. Update a lever's status in the SAME pass its result lands (and the doc's ledger row). Status: open | testing | partial | done | closed | needs-owner.

clock_floor.full: GPU minimum clock in AMD Software (card generates at 600-1350 MHz)
clock_floor.status: closed on Mothership (by reasoning); MEASURED effective on BigHonker NVIDIA
tested: BigHonker 3070 (NVIDIA, Windows), qwen3.6 35B-A3B experts in RAM, 2026-10-17: gpu_clock 1965 (nvidia-smi -lgc) vs unlocked, same launch
clock_floor.result: the owner, 2026-10-01 15:00: the card ramps itself like it does for every game or model; 600-985 MHz is DPM correctly clocking down because the GPU is idle-waiting (load 9-35% in every arm). The clock is a STARVATION GAUGE, not a lever: feed the card and it ramps. A floor would only burn power while it waits.
clock_floor.result_bighonker: 2026-10-17 #34 B10: MEASURED +22% writing - 25.3-26.6 tok/s locked vs 20.3-21.7 unlocked (unlocked -> locked -> unlocked, three locked orders agree, no overlap); unlocked card measured at 450-525 MHz P3 during the answer (idle throttle). CPU and GPU take strict turns (flashnext-profile2b), so GPU segment time is on the critical path. The 10-01 closed verdict above was AMD/Mothership by reasoning (tested: [] then); whether it holds there is untested - the owner to decide on a re-test.

strata_parallel.full: Strata "parallel": N batch slots (engine --batch N): up to N conversations decoded together, expert reads shared across them
strata_parallel.note: 2026-10-18 (the owner: 'Can we cut down on the fixed overhead in any way that's not destructive?'). Short prompts pay a ~0.9 s fixed read cost per request (t = 0.91 s + n / ~1,016 tok/s, from the 4K plateau read and the W1 rows) - Strata streams the experts per prompt chunk (docs\DETAILS.md: 'a 2,048-token chunk is where the prompt path is efficient'; Q2_0 is fixed at --prefill 2048). Agentic turns already avoid most of it through the prompt cache (~96 % reuse per turn, DETAILS.md). Parallel slots raise throughput, not single-answer speed: Strata's BATCHING.md says 'about 10-25% speed per request on this card'. Test: A/B parallel 1 vs 2 - aggregate tok/s AND per-request tok/s - for HAI's multi-user / helper load. Not for menu pricing (single-request is the menu's standard).

cpu_fit_quant.full: the published quant whose CPU-side tensors have AVX2 kernels (K-quants; Q4_0 = llama.cpp's online repack) at the box's speed/quality knee - read the quantizers' model cards + the file's tensor types (header only)
cpu_fit_quant.status: closed for BigHonker's A3B 2026-10-18 (the IQ file stays); open elsewhere (rigby; the 27B per its own file)
tested: BigHonker A3B, same tuned launch (gpu_clock 1965, -t 4 -tb 6, fit 512, b/ub 2048, q8_0 KV, FA, -np 1, ctx 65,536), 4,073-token prompt, writing / reading tok/s | bits/weight | CPU-side MiB: IQ UD-Q3_K_XL 25.6-26.3 / ~1,590 | 3.88 | 11,051 pinned; bartowski Q3_K_M 26.1-26.4 / 1,311-1,504 | 3.85 | 10,507 pinned; bartowski Q4_0 21.2-24.0 / ~1,337 | 4.69 | 14,000 pinned (5 threads 11.5-14.7); unsloth UD-Q4_K_M 22.6-25.0 / 922-957 | 5.11 | 16,106 in ordinary memory
BigHonker qwen3.8:27b (dense), MTP2: lmstudio Q4_K_M 1.88-2.01 (plain 1.73-1.78) vs unsloth Q4_0 1.43-1.52 (6 threads 1.40-1.48)
cpu_fit_quant.result: WRITING FOLLOWS BYTES PER TOKEN, NOT THE QUANT'S KERNELS (2026-10-18; the owner: tuning is quant-specific, don't assume 1-1). The same-size K-quant (Q3_K_M, 3.85 bpw) runs the same as the IQ file (3.88 bpw): 26.1-26.4 vs 25.6-26.3 tok/s, so decode on BigHonker is MEMORY-bound. WITHDRAWN: the earlier reading 'the K kernels are faster per byte' (inferred from UD-Q4_K_M losing less than its size predicted; the cause of that smaller loss was not isolated) and the prediction of ~30 tok/s for Q3_K_M. Larger files lose roughly in proportion (Q4_0 4.69 bpw, UD-Q4_K_M 5.11 bpw). READING follows the CPU-side bytes while the weights sit in pinned CUDA_Host memory, and fell furthest when they did not (UD-Q4_K_M, ordinary memory, 940 vs ~1,590). The IQ file stays the A3B's BigHonker file. The dense 27B: the K-quant Q4_K_M beats Q4_0, and 6 threads = 4 threads, so it is not thread-bound either. Quality is unmeasured for every non-IQ file (the IQ file's role cells sit near their ceilings).

no_host_repack.full: llama.cpp --no-host (bypass the pinned host buffer so the CPU's EXTRA buffer types - the AVX2 8x8 repack - can hold the CPU-side weights); only repack-eligible formats gain (Q4_0, Q4_K, IQ4_NL, Q2_K)
no_host_repack.status: measured on the A3B and the dense 27B (BigHonker, 2026-10-18): writing +10 % (A3B) / +19-25 % (27B Q4_K_M), reading -93 % / -97 % - a per-job option for write-dominated work, not a default
tested: bh-a3b-q40-nohost: bartowski Q4_0 + --no-host, 4 threads, tuned launch: 13,405 MiB repacked with q4_0_8x8 (447 MiB plain); writes 26.19 / 25.64 / 24.11 vs 21.2-24.0 for the same file without it; reads 91.6 / 89.9 tok/s vs ~1,337

bh-q38-27b-nohost2, MTP2, 4 threads: Q4_0 + --no-host writes 2.06-2.15 (vs 1.43-1.52), reads 7.7; lmstudio Q4_K_M + --no-host writes 2.34-2.38 (vs 1.88-2.01), reads 10.2-10.3 (vs 350-378); CPU_REPACK 9,562 / 9,405 MiB
no_host_repack.result: MEASURED 2026-10-18: --no-host lets llama.cpp repack the CPU-side experts (q4_0_8x8) and writing rises ~10 % at equal bytes (24.1-26.2 vs 21.2-24.0) - so decode is not PURELY memory-bound (my 'a repack cannot help' inference was wrong) - but READING collapses ~17x (91 vs ~1,337 tok/s on a 4K prompt: the GPU can no longer borrow the weights from pinned host memory), i.e. a 4K prompt costs ~45 s before the first token. Any role with a long prompt (agentic coding, W1, long documents) loses far more than 10 % writing buys. The dense 27B backup (long contexts) is the same shape, so its --no-host arm is not run. Revisit only for a short-prompt, long-answer role. 2026-10-18 23:28, the dense 27B: repack raises the CPU half's effective rate from ~19.6 to ~28 GB/s (writing +19-25 % on Q4_K_M) but reading falls to ~10 tok/s (a 4K prompt ~7 min). Break-even per agentic turn is ~400 new prompt tokens per 500 written; above that the normal pinned path wins (1K new + 500 out: ~258 s vs ~310 s). RAM verified: ChannelA-DIMM2 + ChannelB-DIMM2, 4000 MT/s configured - the limit is per-core kernel work, not RAM speed (6 threads = 4 threads).

couplings.why: repacked experts are anonymous memory: past RAM they page through the pagefile drive, not mmap's file read-ahead (varied 8.9-11.3 vs 8.9-14.2, 13:38; C: 97% busy, 14:35)
same mechanism at 14.4 GB instead of 31 GB - smaller, still anonymous
the cache only engages on Q2_K-repacked gate tensors with patches\moecache_repack_path.py (else hits=0, stack1 14:30)
repacking all 48 CPU-side layers makes ~50 GB anonymous memory on a 32 GB box - hot48 runs --no-repack
all expert layers CPU-side only fits if they stay file-backed and page from the idle model drive
if the cache carries the reads, extra requests stop growing CPU work - reopen batching on top
every cache miss that inserts is an upload over PCIe - link width/gen bounds insert rate
slots and free margin draw on the same VRAM
slots cost GPU-side layers -> more CPU-side layers -> more RAM; N=35 with 48 slots hit the cliff (4.1 tok/s)
q4_0 KV frees VRAM that becomes slots; more inserts per step = more PCIe traffic per token
more tokens per pass = a bigger union of experts touched -> more page-ins on varied work (+45% warm, +10% varied)
both multiply tokens per pass; the CPU reads the union of all of them
verify passes reuse cached experts - additive
without the cache, aggregate stays flat: each request adds its own experts to CPU work (13:02)
a bigger -ub grows the compute buffer in VRAM, which costs slots or layers
Vulkan prefill trails ROCm (93 vs 174 at equal N); big batches may close part of that
lazy off maps the 27 GB per-layer embedding table into the page cache, competing with experts for RAM
Q2_0 has no repack path: the cook fits RAM but runs plain kernels (warm 14.1 vs 28.4)
a fast non-OS pagefile would make anonymous (repacked / -lm none) experts cheap to page - could flip the repack x mmap conflict
the fitting cook's advantage is avoiding the pagefile drive; a fast pagefile shrinks that advantage
large pages are locked anonymous memory - incompatible with file-backed experts; only for a resident set
a set that fits RAM can be locked in large pages
pinning to physical cores changes the best thread count
1:1 at FCLK 1900 raised the single-CCD read ceiling (warm +6-7%); CPU-side expert time is what a fitting cook also attacks, so re-measure a fitting cook on the new RAM before comparing to old numbers
Vulkan wins generation, ROCm wins prefill - per-job choice
moves attention/DeltaNet to the CPU, the scarce resource (12.5 vs 28.4)
prefetch of routed experts only helps file-backed weights
deep queued reads on the model drive vs synchronous faults on the pagefile drive
-np 1 frees ~1 GB of recurrent-state cache (one more layer or slots); -ub sets the compute buffer that competes with slots
-np 1 is one slot; batching needs -np N, which costs ~1 GB of recurrent state at -np 4
pre-filled slots skip the cold climb (7.7 -> 27 over six generations) that a big cache makes longer
a profile per task family pairs with grouping work by task
both only pay at long context: cached prefixes + cheaper attention over them
long context grows KV in VRAM, which costs slots or layers
fewer wasted thinking tokens and no re-prefill: both cut time-to-answer, not tok/s
thinking text and answer text accept drafts at different rates - acceptance is task-shaped
a cached prefix removes most prefill, shrinking what big batches buy
they STACK (--spec-type draft-mtp,ngram-mod, 2026-10-08); the extra n-gram guesses compete with MTP's for verify passes - on the dense 27B the stack measured no gain
grouping cells by task keeps one task's experts resident instead of re-paging per cell
verify fusion is actually ON in our build before counting it as a win
prefetch reads from the model drive - the idle fast drive is where it belongs
putting a pagefile on F: would make model reads and paging share one drive
hot48: 82% hits, but the 18% misses page from F: one 4 KB fault at a time (queue 2.6, 220 MB/s vs 930 MB/s at queue 27) - prefetching a routed expert in one deep batch is the cure
verify batches of 3 tokens: immediate and deferred sets cover different experts per token, the union can double DDR4 reads; KT applies deferral to single-token decode only
deferral only overlaps if a CPU split can wait on the specific GPU split that produced its input (per-split events), not a full backend synchronize
cached experts run on the GPU anyway; deferral hides the CPU share that remains
same event-based split sync
removes per-split synchronize stalls the scheduler profile counted as waiting
a faster GPU segment changes the CPU's share of each token, so the best thread count can move (BH 10-17: t4 still best at 1965 MHz)
MTP amortises per-token GPU overhead; a clock that cannot park shrinks that overhead, so MTP's gain shrinks (BH: MTP lost both ways)
reading the clock must not load the CPU being measured: nvidia-smi spawned 2x/s cost ~10% on BH's 6 cores; sample in-process (NVML)

--kv-resident 262144 puts the whole KV (~3 GB int8) on the card: expert-cache hit rate fell to ~77 % (flashnext-strata-045-best), writing at depth rose to 64.4 (no KV streaming) - net win on a 24 GB card; on 12-16 GB cards Strata's setup keeps 32K resident for exactly this reason
the table speeds the prefill's dense GEMMs; a bigger chunk (--prefill 8192, the 7900 XTX recipe) gives them bigger, better-tuned shapes - adopted together in the v0.1.45 serving plan
a bigger prompt chunk needs more scratch VRAM (the recipe pairs --prefill 8192 with --vram-reserve-mib 1024)
each batch slot takes ~0.6 GB of VRAM from the expert cache (Strata BATCHING.md); throughput up, per-request speed down (Strata: 'about 10-25% speed per request on this card')

the threads optimum (4 > 5 > 3 >> 6, B10) was measured with IQ experts, where the CPU half may be COMPUTE-bound; K / repacked Q4_0 kernels move it toward DDR4-bandwidth-bound, so the optimum can move - re-check if the new file's write rate lands near the old one

a Q4 file is ~25-30 % larger than the Q3 one: llama.cpp's fitter (fit 512) puts fewer layers on the 8 GB card, so more of every token is read from RAM - the speed gain from fast kernels is partly paid back here
MTP's verify cost depends on what each extra token reads from RAM; a faster CPU half changes the break-even (dense 27B: drafting attacks the bandwidth floor; split A3B: it lost at the old file)

-ub 2048 reading (2.4x on BigHonker) works because the GPU borrows pinned CPU-side weights per batch; --no-host takes the weights out of pinned memory, so reading is expected to fall - the price of faster CPU kernels
only repack-eligible formats (Q4_0, Q4_K, IQ4_NL, Q2_K) gain from --no-host; the IQ3_XXS/IQ4_XS experts of the tuned A3B file have no repack path, so for that file it only costs the pinned placement
repacked 8x8 kernels do more work per memory read, moving the CPU half from compute- toward bandwidth-bound; the thread optimum measured on plain kernels can move
